candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — eating disorders / bulimia nervosa
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize the defining behavioral pattern of bulimia nervosa and distinguish it from binge-eating disorder, restrictive eating disorders, and occasional overeating.

options.A: Recurrent binge-eating episodes followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting, fasting, or excessive exercise.
options.B: Recurrent binge-eating episodes without recurrent compensatory behaviors intended to prevent weight gain.
options.C: Persistent energy restriction resulting in significantly low body weight without recurrent binge-eating episodes.
options.D: Occasional overeating during stress without recurrent loss-of-control binges or compensatory behaviors.

candidate.rationale: Bulimia nervosa is characterized by recurrent binge eating with loss of control followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors intended to prevent weight gain, such as self-induced vomiting, laxative or diuretic misuse, fasting, or excessive exercise. A is the only option that contains both defining features. Body weight alone does not establish or exclude the disorder.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Bulimia nervosa involves recurrent binge eating with loss of control followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, laxative/diuretic use, fasting, or excessive exercise.
